segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Hi, this is Dana from North Ridge. We opened ticket 48219 this morning because last night’s user import only brought over 86 of 124 employees for our April 1 go-live.

segments.speaker: Agent
segments.text: Yeah, I’m looking at that now. I see the import file uploaded at 7:12 p.m. Central, and the first 86 rows processed. Let me check the admin console for the remaining rows.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. The missing users are all in the Minneapolis office, if that helps. I’m a little surprised we had to catch this ourselves; it seems like the system could have flagged that only part of the file loaded.

segments.speaker: Agent
segments.text: Understood. I see what happened: row 87 has a department value with an extra comma, so the parser stopped there instead of continuing. I can correct the delimiter issue and rerun the same file on my side.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Please don’t send welcome emails yet. We’re holding those until Thursday morning.

segments.speaker: Agent
segments.text: Yep, I’ll keep invitations off. I’m rerunning the import now with notifications disabled, and I’ll verify the count against 124 before I update the ticket.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. We also need their manager assignments to come through, not just the profiles.

segments.speaker: Agent
segments.text: They’re included in the file. The rerun just finished: 124 active users, 124 manager assignments, zero invitations sent. I’m adding the import summary to ticket 48219.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Thanks. Can you leave the corrected file attached there too? Our HR coordinator will want to compare it.

segments.speaker: Agent
segments.text: Done. I attached it as north-ridge-users-corrected-0329.csv and noted the original row that caused the stop. You should be set for Thursday.
